# Week of 2026-10-05 — Compass's Review

The headline this week isn't the -$200 — it's that there's almost nothing to coach from. Four trades, no setup labels, no process scores, no emotion or mistake tags. The data skeleton is there; the connective tissue that makes a journal useful isn't. That's the real story of week one.

## Performance
- Net P&L: -$200.00 (-0.02%)

- Win rate: 50.0% · Avg R: -0.50 · Profit factor: 0.71
- vs last week: First active week on record; no prior baseline to compare against.

## Process
- Process score avg: — (no scores recorded)
- A+ setups taken: 0
- Risk-cap breaches: 0 (overrides used: 0)
- Discipline lockouts hit: 0
- No setup labels were applied to any of the four trades. Without them, there's no way to tell whether these were planned entries or reactive ones.

## Setups
- All four trades logged under no setup label — best and worst comparison isn't possible this week.
- The two losses on NVDA totaled -7R; the two winners on AAPL and TSLA returned +5R. The net -2R on the week came entirely from the NVDA pair. Whether that's a setup problem, a sizing problem, or a stop problem is unreadable without labels and process scores.

## Psychology
- Process tagging was thin this week — limits what I can read. No emotion or mistake tags were applied to any trade. That's not a character flaw; it's a data gap. The journal can't surface patterns it wasn't given.

- Max daily drawdown: not resolvable
